findings.summary: Stored data callbacks initially added aliases around the existing native-function-body lifecycle even though both paths require the same scope, return and capture handling; the aliases were removed and stored callbacks reuse beginNativeFunctionBody/endNativeFunctionBody directly.

Dynamic asset packaging compiled the same runtime expression while probing both a direct candidate and a directory; directory discovery now runs first while network-scheme prefixes continue through the static URL path.

Dynamic pixel texture updates copied a complete RGBA vector again while synchronizing SpriteRenderer bindings; the update now moves pixels into shared backing once and assigns that backing to every bound layer.

Function-valued class fields were excluded from stored-data lowering in both the caller and signature mapper; one origin-aware ancestor traversal now covers inline and aliased callback signatures without duplicating the policy.

The standalone effect renderer already links the shared SDL image dependency, so its file-texture decoder now reuses the same pal_sdl implementation gate as PBR and sprite renderers instead of requiring renderer-specific decoding code.
